extracted.intended_audience: research teams and institutional research administrators preparing applications to the DOE BES Energy Frontier Research Centers (EFRC) NOFO DE-FOA-0003614
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a pre-application and full application for the DOE Office of Science, Basic Energy Sciences Energy Frontier Research Centers (EFRC) Notice of Funding Opportunity DE-FOA-0003614, meeting topic-specific responsiveness, eligibility, and administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Application Requirement and Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A Pre-Application is required. Pre-Applications must be submitted by an authorized institutional representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that are submitted by applicants that have not submitted a required pre-application will be declined without further review. Pre-applications must be submitted by an authorized institutional representative. Applicants are encouraged to submit pre-applications well before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Institution Consistency Between Pre-Application and Application
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead institution identified in an application must be the same lead institution identified in the required pre-application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is received for which the lead organization has changed since submission of the pre-application, then the application may be declined without further review. The lead PI (EFRC Director) should not be changed unless unavoidable and only minor edits should be made, if necessary, to the title of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Number of Submissions (Institution & Individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant institutions are limited to no more than three pre-applications or applications as the lead institution. An individual may not be named as the PI (EFRC Director) on more than one pre-application or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no limit to the number of applications on which an institution appears as a subrecipient. Should DOE receive submissions in excess of the applicable limits, DOE may request clarifying information or consider the latest received submissions to be the institution’s intended submissions. Pre-applications in excess may be discouraged; applications in excess may be declined without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFRC Director (PI) Eligibility and Appointment Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EFRC Directors must be in a permanent or indefinitely extensible position at the applicant institution; individuals in term-limited appointments (adjunct, visiting, fellows, etc.) are not eligible. EFRC Directors on university led applications must be in a tenured position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part-time permanent positions are eligible. Joint-appointment individuals are eligible if work will be performed at the applicant institution and the EFRC Director is a paid employee on the applicant institution’s payroll. Individuals receiving more than half of their salary and benefits from a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory may not be named as the EFRC Director in an application submitted by an applicant other than a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Scope: Basic and Use-Inspired Basic Research Only (No Applied Research/Technology Development)
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of the EFRC program is on fundamental scientific research; applications to this NOFO must not propose applied research and technology development activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This NOFO does not support an applicant’s commercial activity. Applications that propose research related to current commercial activity or current customer needs may be declined without merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: For-Profit Applicant Appendix Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All for-profit applicants must include a description, not to exceed 200 words, of how their proposed work will advance scientific understanding of a basic and fundamental nature as an appendix to the Project Narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is to ensure proposed work is within the NOFO's basic research scope; failing to provide such justification risks being found unresponsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Domestic Subrecipient Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may propose non-domestic entities as subrecipients, but successful applications that propose non-domestic subrecipients must include a detailed demonstration of how the proposed non-domestic subrecipients possess skills, resources, and abilities that do not exist among potential domestic subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration must be sufficiently detailed to justify inclusion of non-domestic partners; lack of adequate justification may affect responsiveness or selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing Not Required and Not Considered in Merit Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing for basic and fundamental research is not required pursuant to an exclusion from the requirements of Section 988 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005. Cost sharing will not be considered as a factor during merit review or award selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost sharing is not required of DOE/NNSA National Laboratories, other Federal agencies, another Federal agency’s FFRDC, or their subcontractors at any tier. Note: laboratories or agencies may impose internal cost-sharing policies on their contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE/NNSA National Laboratory and FFRDC Participation Rules and Funding Mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE/NNSA National Laboratories are eligible to submit applications and may be proposed as subrecipients; non-DOE/NNSA FFRDCs are not eligible to submit but may be subrecipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a DOE/NNSA National Laboratory is recommended for funding as a lead applicant, funding will be provided through the DOE Field-Work Proposal System and work will be conducted under the laboratory’s contract with DOE; administrative provisions of this NOFO will not apply to the laboratory or laboratory subcontractor. If recommended for funding as a proposed subrecipient, the value of the proposed subaward will be removed from the prime applicant’s award and provided through the Field-Work Proposal System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Responsiveness — BES Reports Topics and PRD/PRO Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: In BES Reports Topics, applicants must address priority research directions (PRD) and opportunities (PRO) identified in listed reports; each report may impose restrictions on which PRDs/PROs new and renewal applications may respond to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NOFO lists the reports applicants must draw from (e.g., Foundational Science to Accelerate Nuclear Energy Innovation; Controlling Subsurface Fractures and Fluid Flow; Basic Research Needs for Next Generation Electrical Energy Storage; Basic Research Needs for Transformative Manufacturing; Basic Research Needs for Microelectronics; BES Roundtable on Opportunities for Quantum Computing in Chemical and Materials Sciences; BES Roundtable on Opportunities for Basic Research for Next-Generation Quantum Systems). Examples of report-specific restrictions: Basic Research Needs for Next Generation Electrical Energy Storage — renewal applications may respond to all PRDs; new applications may respond only to PRD 2 or PRD 3. Applicants must follow report-specific PRO/PRD restrictions listed in Section III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Topic: Controlling Quantum Phenomena to Enable Unconventional Computing Paradigms
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must demonstrate and establish novel quantum-phenomenon-based computing paradigms suitable for data intensive computing while also advancing fundamental understanding of computation and learning as a physical process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A co-design approach integrating emerging quantum functionalities into unconventional compute frameworks is required. Demonstration of scalability must be supported by full circuit analyses, system-level insights, model devices, and/or computational methods. Possible paradigms include analog, probabilistic, nonlinear, reservoir, and quantum neural network computing; encouraged application areas include in-memory, neuromorphic, reservoir, Boltzmann, optical, or continuous-variable quantum computing. Exclusions: applications focused on discrete variable quantum computing or phenomena in conventional and/or bulk materials are not responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Topic: Development and Workflow Integration of AI/ML Models for Materials and Chemistry Discovery Science
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic invites development of physics- and chemistry-informed AI/ML methods to address a well-defined, BES-relevant scientific challenge using structured, multimodal data, with models applied and validated on real experimental data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches must embed scientific knowledge into model architecture and close the loop with experiments; agentic AI elements may be incorporated. Exclusions: AI/ML models focused on instrument operations through hardware controls; AI-assisted/automated experiments; digital twins; AI models that reproduce known laws from existing datasets; AI models focusing only on combining existing AI/ML tools; projects focusing only on demonstrating AI-ready datasets (data processing, compression, curation). Proposed models must be validated on real experimental data (not only simulated inputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Topic: Emergent Phenomena of Complex Chemical Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Invites cross-disciplinary research to create, control, and exploit emergent phenomena and non-equilibrium processes at the molecular level to advance energy-relevant chemical systems, with emphasis on dynamics, component integration, and energy-efficient chemical manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three emphasis areas: (1) elucidating dynamics at component and systems levels (stimuli-responsiveness, field/gradient formation, energy dissipation, kinetic asymmetry); (2) mastering component integration under far-from-equilibrium conditions (ensemble effects, interface structure/energy transfer, co-design); (3) transforming chemical manufacturing via energy-efficient systems (electrochemical, light-driven, plasma-mediated, non-thermal, combined energy inputs). Exclusions: research based on whole biological cells; projects predominantly focused on hydrogen production; applied research with primary focus on device development, reactor design, process optimization, or scale-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Topic: Fundamental Science for Critical Minerals and Materials (CMM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks multidisciplinary research to identify molecular mechanisms promoting CMM supply chain availability, considering source variability and producing outputs compatible with supply chain processing needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis areas include controlling impacts of source heterogeneity in initial isolation, exploiting dynamics of non-linear emergent system properties for selective capture and release, and other fundamental mechanisms to improve isolation, extraction, and processing compatibility. Proposals must consider sequential chemical/physical transformations and potential CMM loss throughout the supply chain; demonstrate how approaches account for source variability and conversion to process-compatible forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability, Validation, and Experimental Requirements for Topic Responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Many topics require demonstration of scalability and validation on real experimental systems/data rather than simulation alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Quantum phenomena topic requires scalability supported by circuit analyses, model devices, or computational methods; AI/ML topic requires application and validation on real experimental data; proposals that do not provide required experimental validation or scalable pathway may be deemed unresponsive to the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Amounts, Project Period, and Funding Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected award size is $3,000,000 to $4,500,000 per award per year (total $12M to $18M for a 4-year period). DOE anticipates total available funding and an expected average award size of ~$4,000,000 per award per year after the first year. Project period is four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For renewal applications DOE may consider limited-term renewal awards with annual funding below the $3,000,000 floor to allow completion and orderly closeout. For new applications Year 1 funding may be less than subsequent years recognizing ramp-up. DOE is under no obligation to cover costs for application preparation and may fund none, some, or all meritorious applications depending on appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Compliance: Registrations, Notifications, and Submission Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to register in all required systems (e.g., Grants.gov, SAM.gov) as soon as possible and follow submission instructions; applicants are strongly encouraged to inform EFRC@science.doe.gov if teaming arrangements, proposed personnel, or anticipated title change between pre-application and application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with registration or submission instructions may affect acceptance. The NOFO provides detailed submission instructions and deadlines (pre-application and application response dates). Applicants should follow the address/request application package and UEI/SAM requirements in Section V.
